item.title: Teenage Shi denies world record holder as China sweeps race walk golds
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 23 (Xinhua) -- China swept both half-marathon race walk titles at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Wednesday, with Shi Shengji claiming the first athletics gold of the Games before Yang Liujing won the women's crown. The half-marathon race walk, contested over 21.0975 kilometers, is being held at the Asian Games for the first time. It replaced the 20km race walk on the program following World Athletics' change to the standard senior road race walking distances this season. Shi and Toshikazu Yamanishi passed the 5km mark together in 19 minutes and 44 seconds. Shi then moved clear and was leading alone by 10km. Yamanishi and compatriot Kento Yoshikawa each had to serve a two-minute penalty after receiving three red cards. The 19-year-old finished the men's race in one hour, 23 minutes and 32 seconds, beating Japan's world record holder Yamanishi, who took silver in 1:28:01. South Korea's Choe Byeongkwang won bronze in 1:28:35. Shi said his plan had been to follow the leaders for much of the race, but he decided to take the lead when he saw their pace drop. He credited close attention to technique in training for avoiding the penalties that affected several rivals. Speaking about the Chinese team, Yamanishi said: "I have long been aware of the strength of Chinese race walkers. Many talented young athletes have emerged since last year in particular. We are learning from them while also challenging them." Yoshikawa, who finished seventh in the 20km race walk at last year's world championships, placed fourth. China's Li Chenjie was disqualified after receiving four red cards. Chin Man Kit of Hong Kong, China finished fifth in 1:34:26. Chinese Taipei's Lo Sheng-qin and Chan Yung-kuei placed sixth and eighth, respectively. In the women's race, Yang and teammate Jiang Yunyan led from the start. Yang held on to win in 1:33:40 after Jiang was sent to the penalty area. Kazakhstan's Kristina Morozova moved into second and finished in 1:35:25, one second ahead of bronze medalist Jiang. Yang said the two Chinese athletes had planned to work together. Being left alone in front as fatigue set in was one of the hardest parts of her race, she added. The athletics competition will run through Sept. 29. ■

item.title: China holds off Japan for third straight men's gymnastics team gold
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 23 (Xinhua) -- China defended its men's team title in gymnastics at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Wednesday, claiming a third straight championship in the event. The Chinese team of Zhang Boheng, Lan Xingyu, Zou Jingyuan, Sun Wei and Tian Hao won the title with 255.095 points, followed by Japan with 253.826 for silver and Chinese Taipei with 239.896 for bronze. It was China's second gold medal here in gymnastics, following Zhang's men's all-around title on Monday. The gap stayed tight in the opening floor exercise, where Japan's Tokyo Olympic all-around champion Daiki Hashimoto topped the field with 14.000, followed by China's Tian Hao with 13.966. On pommel horse, Paris Olympic all-around champion Shinnosuke Oka, first up for Japan, fell off the apparatus and managed just 12.533. Hashimoto followed with a strong 14.466, but three solid routines from the Chinese trio kept China narrowly ahead on aggregate. The crowd's excitement peaked during a scintillating rings battle between China and Japan, with neither side landing a dismount error as the two teams swept the top six spots. China's Lan Xingyu posted the event's top score of 15.200 - a 6.0 difficulty, 9.100 execution and 0.1 bonus - ahead of Japan's Kiichi Kaneta on 14.900. On vault, Oka was the only gymnast among the competitors from the two teams to suffer a major error, while Hashimoto and Asian Games all-around champion Zhang both delivered strong routines, tying at 14.733 (Hashimoto later made a successful inquiry to add 0.1 points). Zou Jingyuan, the Paris Olympic and four-time world champion on parallel bars, was in dominant form on the apparatus, scoring 15.400 on a 6.0 difficulty and 9.300 execution - a full 0.834 clear of second-placed Oka. China carried a 1.934-point cushion into the final rotation, high bar. The horizontal bar competition swung back and forth: China's Sun, first up, suffered a fall, but Japan's Oka also faltered soon after. Hashimoto then delivered a near-flawless routine for 15.233. Needing just 12.931 to seal the gold for China, Zhang - competing last - made sure there would be no repeat of his Paris Olympic heartbreak, scoring 14.200 to lift China to a final total of 255.095, 1.269 points clear of Japan. Asked about Sun Wei's fall on the horizontal bar, China's team captain Zhang Boheng said the team's preparation had left them ready to absorb a setback without losing composure. "We did extremely thorough, scientific preparation heading into the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. Even when a small mistake happens, we don't panic - we adjust immediately," Zhang said at the post-competition press conference. "Across the whole competition we had 18 routines to get through, and with that kind of workload, one or two slips are within the range we can accept. Sun is a veteran who holds himself to a very high standard, so we told him not to worry - we still had it in hand," Zhang added. Zhang said the team title meant even more to him than his individual all-around gold two days earlier. "We put out every bit of difficulty we had. We'd trained this at home countless times, all building toward this gold medal today. So when I finished my final routine, it wasn't just me who was excited - everyone was," Zhang said. ■

item.title: Dear Word | What can a "BOAT" tell us about China-U.S. relations?
item.description:

Chinese President Xi Jinping has on several occasions compared China-U.S. relations to a giant ship navigating winds and waves. In English, we say, "We're in the same boat." In Chinese, there's a similar expression: 同舟共济 (tóng zhōu gòng jì). But it goes one step further - not just sharing the same boat, but helping each other through the storm. #DearWord #ChineseCulture

item.title: Xi builds friendship across the Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
* Over the years, Xi has personally stayed in close touch with people from all walks of life in the United States through meetings, visits, letters and speeches. * In November 2023, Xi announced in San Francisco that 50,000 young Americans would be invited to China on exchange and study programs in the next five years. The target was reached in just two and a half years, as young Americans traveled across China, met their Chinese peers and experienced the country's history, culture and development firsthand. BEIJING, Sept. 23 (Xinhua) -- "The foundation of China-U.S. relations lies among the people, the hope is in the people, the future lies in the youth, and the vitality lies in sub-national areas," Chinese President Xi Jinping once said. For many years, Xi has consistently championed people-to-people friendship between China and the United States, seeking to bring the Chinese and Americans ever closer and rally stronger public support for the two countries to get along. BRINGING HEARTS CLOSER China-U.S. relations are widely regarded as the world's most important bilateral relationship. On how the two major countries can deepen cooperation and navigate differences and challenges, Xi has highlighted the vital role of people-to-people friendship and cultural exchanges. Speaking to the American public, Xi has often stressed, "state-to-state relations ultimately rely on the support of the people and serve the people." He once used his fingers to form the Chinese character "ren," meaning "person" to illustrate how the Chinese and American people should support each other in Seattle during his state visit to the United States in 2015. Over the years, Xi has personally stayed in close touch with people from all walks of life in the United States through meetings, visits, letters and speeches. During his visit to San Francisco in 2023, Xi set aside time to meet with representatives of Americans who had long supported friendship with China. Smiling, he warmly shook hands and exchanged greetings with each of them. On Monday, just two days ahead of his state visit to the United States, Xi replied to students from 10 U.S. universities who wrote to him after attending youth exchanges in China. He encouraged the students to join the vast number of young people in both countries in striving to carry forward, uphold, and advance China-U.S. friendly cooperation, and work together to foster mutual understanding and affinity between the two peoples. "The peoples of China and the United States are both great peoples. Achieving the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again can go hand in hand. We can help each other succeed and advance the well-being of the whole world," Xi once said. FRIENDSHIP SPANNING DECADES Over the decades, Xi's encounters with people from across American society have become cherished chapters in the story of friendship between the Chinese and Americans. Recalling his visit to the Midwestern U.S. state of Iowa 41 years ago, Xi said he was warmly received, and those wonderful memories remain fresh in his mind to this day. In the spring of 1985, Xi, then a young official, led a delegation to Iowa. During the visit, he spent three days in Muscatine, a city in rural eastern Iowa, where he stayed with local hosts. Through long hours of friendly exchanges, they gained a genuine understanding of the people living across the Pacific. "You were the first group of Americans I came into contact with," Xi told his Iowa friends in 2012 when visiting Iowa once again as China's vice president. "To me, you are America." Today, 2911 Bonnie Drive, the place where he stayed, has been turned into a museum and renamed the Sino-U.S. Friendship House, while Muscatine has become a "city of friendship." For friendship to endure, youth exchanges and educational cooperation matter. "Young people, full of vitality and dreams, represent the future and hope of China-U.S. relations and of the world," Xi said, describing education as "a bridge linking the people of China and the United States." In 1993, Xi, then secretary of the Fuzhou Municipal Committee of the Communist Party of China, visited Lincoln High School during a trip to Tacoma, the state of Washington, as Fuzhou and Tacoma explored establishing sister-city ties. Twenty-two years later in 2015, he returned to the school during his state visit to the United States, presenting books on China and table tennis equipment and encouraging students to visit his country for "a more comprehensive and profound understanding of China." The following year, more than 100 Lincoln students and teachers traveled to China. In November 2023, Xi announced in San Francisco that 50,000 young Americans would be invited to China on exchange and study programs in the next five years. The target was reached in just two and a half years, as young Americans traveled across China, met their Chinese peers and experienced the country's history, culture and development firsthand. BUILDING BRIDGES "We should build more bridges and pave more roads for people-to-people interactions. We must not erect barriers or create a chilling effect," Xi once said. Over the years, Xi has worked to expand channels of contact between the two countries, including through exchanges in the business sector. During his 2015 U.S. visit, he toured companies like Microsoft and Boeing. He has on many occasions met with U.S. business leaders and attended China-U.S. business roundtables and dialogues. Most recently, in May, Xi met U.S. entrepreneurs accompanying Trump to China. He expressed confidence that U.S. companies would enjoy even broader prospects in China. China's door "will only open wider," he added. Xi has also emphasized exchanges between the two countries at local levels. He has attended events such as the China-U.S. Governors' Forum and met with U.S. governors on many occasions. Today, the two countries have 50 pairs of sister provinces and states, and 238 pairs of sister cities. On June 5, such a network brought hundreds of representatives together in San Francisco for the 8th China-U.S. Sister Cities Conference. The long history of friendship is a shared legacy of the two peoples. At various events, Xi has recounted stories of the Flying Tigers, the Hump route, the Doolittle Raid rescue and Ping-Pong Diplomacy. He called on the two peoples to carry forward the friendship that "withstood the test of blood and fire," and urged younger generations, in particular, to "draw wisdom and strength from history." Noting that China-U.S. relations concern the well-being of the over 1.7 billion people of both countries and affect the interests of the over 8 billion people of the world, Xi said both sides should rise up to this historic responsibility. That view is echoed by Jeffrey Greene, chairman of the Sino-American Aviation Heritage Foundation. The United States and China "have a duty to humanity to cooperate," he said. (Video reporters: Xiong Maoling, Jia Fan and Hu Yousong; Video editors: Mu Xuyao, Liu Xiaorui and Yu Jiaming)■

item.title: Global economic growth projected at 2.9 pct in 2026: OECD
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
PARIS, Sept. 23 (Xinhua) -- Global economic growth is projected to be 2.9 percent in 2026 and 3.0 percent in 2027, according to the Economic Outlook Interim Report released by the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) on Wednesday. Growth in the advanced G20 economies, as well as in the G20 emerging-market economies, is projected to remain broadly stable, the report said. G20 headline inflation is expected to rise from 3.4 percent in 2025 to 4.1 percent in 2026, before easing to 3.6 percent in 2027, according to the report. In the advanced G20 economies, headline inflation is projected to rise from 2.5 percent in 2025 to 3.2 percent in 2026, before falling to 2.6 percent in 2027, while in emerging-market G20 economies it is expected to increase from 4.1 percent to 4.8 percent before easing to 4.3 percent. The OECD noted that the projections are based on a technical assumption that Brent crude prices and TTF gas prices will peak in the fourth quarter of 2026 and then decline steadily through the end of 2027. The assumed Brent crude price path is broadly consistent with the "short disruption" scenario in the OECD's June 2026 Economic Outlook, while the assumed gas price path is about 60 percent higher. Persistent uncertainty over the evolution of the conflict in the Middle East remains a key risk to the baseline projections, the OECD warned, adding that constraints on exports through the Strait of Hormuz, additional disruptions to alternative export routes such as the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, or further significant damage to energy production facilities in the region could prompt a further sustained rise in energy prices and potentially lead to shortages of key commodities, particularly in net importing countries. Low European gas reserves and uncertain scope for sustained further reductions in oil inventories in some countries could exacerbate supply disruption risks. "Further monetary policy rate adjustments may be needed," the OECD said, noting that faced with renewed energy price shocks, stronger-than-expected demand pressures, and above-target inflation in many economies, central banks need to ensure that underlying inflation pressures are durably contained. The OECD also called for further structural policy reforms to help economies cope with future supply shocks, including diversifying energy supply, improving energy efficiency, enhancing product and labor market adjustment, and ensuring workers have adaptable skills. ■

item.title: Economic Watch: Pinglu Canal boosts China-ASEAN connectivity, win-win cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
BEIJING, Sept. 23 (Xinhua) -- Using the newly opened Pinglu Canal, a cargo ship carrying potassium fertilizer from Laos arrived at a plant in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region five to seven days sooner than using traditional routes. Using the same canal, 3.1 tonnes of Guangxi specialty tea arrived in Vietnam in a much shorter time, cutting hundreds of kilometers off the journey and eliminating multiple transfer, waiting and loading procedures. The 134.2-kilometer canal, stretching from Hengzhou in Guangxi to the Beibu Gulf, opened on Sept. 16. It is the closest maritime outlet for much of southwest China. "Steel and machinery equipment from southwest China including Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan and Chongqing can now reach ASEAN markets more easily through the Pinglu Canal, while ASEAN products can also flow more efficiently into China's vast domestic market," said Du Jianjun, chairman of China Railway Eryuan Engineering Group. For instance, the new waterway will significantly cut logistics costs for Thai goods entering China -- including computers, fruits and rubber products -- allowing them to reach consumers in southwestern China faster than ever before. Philippine exporters of fresh fruit and seafood with short shelf lives stand to benefit too, as the canal cuts transit times and improves delivery efficiency. The Pinglu Canal will help further boost trade growth between ASEAN and China, said Ngeow Chow Bing, director of the Institute of China Studies at University of Malaya. China and ASEAN have been each other's largest trading partner for years. Bilateral trade surpassed 1 trillion U.S. dollars for the first time in 2025, reaching 1.05 trillion U.S. dollars. In the first eight months of this year, bilateral trade totaled 862.75 billion U.S. dollars, up 25.6 percent year on year. On the very day the canal opened, a cargo ship carrying knock-down (KD) vehicle kits from Dongfeng Liuzhou Motor passed through the waterway bound for an assembly line in Cambodia. Describing the canal as a golden corridor, Liu Xiaoping, an executive of Dongfeng Liuzhou, said the company will incorporate the canal into its regular export logistics system. Official data showed intermediate goods now account for two thirds of bilateral trade between China and ASEAN. The two sides are moving beyond simple "buying and selling" to building shared industrial ecosystems. As intermediate goods and processed products move more efficiently, China's relationship with ASEAN is shifting toward a production partnership, said Zhou Yamin, a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, noting that the change will significantly promote regional economic integration. Experts said the canal's long-term significance lies not just in what it transports, but in what it will attract in the future. As logistics costs fall, new investment is expected to flow into industries related to the canal, including warehousing, processing, cold chain and industrial parks. Capital, technology, talent and labor from southwestern China and ASEAN will converge to spur growth and generate new employment. The canal's opening comes at a moment of steady development of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area (FTA). The Version 1.0 of the FTA was fully established in 2010, with zero tariffs on more than 90 percent of goods. A subsequent Version 2.0 protocol took full effect in 2019, expanding services and investment access. In October 2025, a 3.0 Upgrade Protocol was signed, extending cooperation into digital trade, green economy, standards and supply chains. Against that backdrop, the Pinglu Canal is more than a feat of engineering. Experts said it is the physical expression of decades of deepening economic ties and the artery through which the next chapter of China-ASEAN win-win cooperation will flow. ■

item.title: Xinhua Headlines: China secures bumper harvest with stable fertilizer supply, smart farming
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
* Against tightening global fertilizer supply rattled by geopolitical headwinds, China's targeted measures have secured agricultural supplies and underpinned national food security. * Complementing stable material supplies, advanced agricultural technology has helped China mitigate the impact of natural disasters and lift grain yields, helping secure a resilient autumn harvest. * China's grain production has stayed on firm footing this year. Official data released in July put summer grain output at 150.7 billion kilograms, up 0.7 percent year on year, marking the first time the harvest has topped 150 billion kilograms. The country is on track to meet its annual grain output target of around 700 billion kilograms. WUHAN/HARBIN, Sept. 23 (Xinhua) -- As combine harvesters bring the autumn harvest to a close across central China's Hubei Province, local farmer Fu Pengcheng is preparing his 1,000 mu (66.7 hectares) of farmland for winter wheat rotation, reassured by stable fertilizer supplies heading into the upcoming planting season. The 42-year-old farmer has stockpiled 40 tonnes of fertilizer at 3,065 yuan (454.29 U.S. dollars) per tonne. "Though slightly higher compared with last year, the price is still reasonable," said Fu, adding that his county has ample fertilizer stocks for him to replenish at any time. Like Fu, farmers across China today no longer have to scramble for fertilizer or stockpile it during the busy farming season, nor do they have to worry about fertilizer price spikes. Against tightening global fertilizer supply rattled by geopolitical headwinds, the country's targeted measures have secured agricultural supplies and underpinned national food security. China's grain production has stayed on firm footing this year. Official data released in July put summer grain output at 150.7 billion kilograms, up 0.7 percent year on year, marking the first time the harvest has topped 150 billion kilograms. The country is on track to meet its annual grain output target of around 700 billion kilograms. STABLE FERTILIZER SUPPLY Fertilizer, an essential input for grain farming, faces severe global supply strains in 2026. Escalating geopolitical tensions in the Gulf region have disrupted vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical export route for fertilizers. The disruption has severely fragmented global fertilizer supply chains. The World Bank forecasts a 31 percent overall surge in global fertilizer prices for 2026. Most economies are grappling with fertilizer shortages and soaring farming costs, which pose growing threats to their food security. As the world's major fertilizer producer and consumer, China has rolled out targeted measures to counter global market volatility, stabilize domestic fertilizer supply and underpin food security against external challenges. Early this year, China's top economic regulator issued a guideline to ensure year-round fertilizer supply and price stability for spring plowing, requiring multiple departments to coordinate efforts to boost fertilizer production, cut farming costs, optimize reserve management and promote scientific fertilization practices. Across the country, fertilizer producers have responded by expanding output and diversifying procurement. At the production park of Hubei Yihua Group Co., Ltd. in Yichang, Hubei Province, intelligent production lines are running at full speed. Bags of fertilizer are automatically filled, sealed and palletized before being quickly transferred to the finished product warehouse through an intelligent loading system. Faced with sharp price increases and supply fluctuations of fertilizer raw materials such as sulfur, the company has actively expanded diversified overseas procurement channels to stabilize external import sources. It has also deepened cooperation with major central state-owned enterprises such as Sinopec and PetroChina, signing long-term raw material procurement agreements to lock in preferential procurement terms and supply quotas. In the first eight months of this year, the company's total domestic fertilizer output reached 2.95 million tonnes. Beyond corporate efforts, China's systematic reserve and distribution network forms the backbone of fertilizer supply security. The country has a commercial fertilizer reserve system, with a full-spectrum reserve framework covering nitrogen, phosphorus, compound, potash and disaster-relief fertilizers across major agricultural provinces, said Ye Xingqing, a researcher with the Development Research Center of the State Council. A nationwide agricultural supply network further ensures efficient distribution, with over 4,800 agricultural input enterprises and 280,000 grassroots service outlets across rural areas. During this year's spring plowing season, China released more than 10 million tonnes of state commercial fertilizer reserves, strongly supporting stable grain production. Thanks to coordinated policy regulation, expanded industrial output and industry self-discipline, domestic fertilizer prices have stayed largely stable this year, in stark contrast to sharp global price hikes driven by geopolitical conflicts, said Wang Xiaoxue, an official with the China Agricultural Means of Production Association. SMART FARMING TECHNOLOGY Complementing stable material supplies, advanced agricultural technology has helped China mitigate the impact of natural disasters and lift grain yields, helping secure a resilient autumn harvest. Henan, a key grain-producing province in central China, has leveraged drone monitoring and smart field management to improve disaster response after Typhoon Dolphin struck in August. Rather than sending teams to inspect fields on foot, researchers use surveillance drones to send real-time soil and waterlogging data to smart platforms. This allows fast drainage and targeted loss control. Wang Qiang, an associate professor at Henan Agricultural University, led the practice at an agricultural demonstration park, deploying drones to assess damage instead of wading into fields. His smart farm project in Luohe City of Henan, uses patrol drones to stream real-time field data to a smart management platform. "We spot waterlogged areas and activate drainage promptly to curb losses," Wang said. He added that agricultural demonstration sites nationwide let farmers test new technologies on the ground. These projects speed up the upgrade of China's farm machinery fleet and make it smarter. The province has achieved a 90-percent comprehensive mechanization rate for crop planting and harvesting, with wheat and corn production fully mechanized. Nationwide, BeiDou-guided autonomous tractors, intelligent seeders, automated water-fertilizer irrigation systems and straw balers now cover the entire planting, management and harvesting cycle, powering precision farming. In Heilongjiang, China's largest grain-producing province, autumn harvesting is underway. Its overall farm planting and harvesting mechanization rate has led the country for years, surpassing 99 percent. Widely seen as a cornerstone of national food security, the province is rolling out new technology to boost per-hectare yields and crop quality. The province deployed over 25,000 precision seeders and 33,000 crop-protection drones this year to lift farm operation standards and efficiency, said Zhu Huasheng, deputy director of the provincial agriculture and rural affairs department. Official figures also show Heilongjiang has dispatched more than 26,000 agricultural officials and experts to the fields so far this year, guiding farmers to adopt new technologies. Cheng Guoqiang, dean of the National School of Food Security Strategy at Renmin University of China, said that in a year of tightening global grain supplies, China's steady grain production has helped stabilize global market expectations. ■ (Reporting by Qiang Lijing, Fang Ning, Rong Jiaojiao, Tian Zhongquan, Sun Xiaoyu, Hou Wenkun and Yuan Yueming; Video reporters: Fang Yadong, Hou Wenkun, Tian Zhongquan, and Sun Xiaoyu; Video editors: Li Ziwei, Zhao Xiaoqing and Roger Lott.)

item.title: Xi sends congratulatory letter to 48th WorldSkills Competition
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
BEIJING, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter on Tuesday to the 48th WorldSkills Competition. Xi noted that a new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation is advancing rapidly, exerting a profound impact on global skills development. Closely aligned with the needs of industries, the WorldSkills Competition provides a useful platform for skilled professionals from various countries to hone their skills and learn from each other, Xi said. Xi stressed that China will take the opportunity of hosting this year's competition to encourage and guide more workers, especially young people, to pursue a path to success through skills. "China is willing to strengthen exchanges and cooperation with all parties, promote the development of the WorldSkills movement, and better contribute to global economic growth and the improvement of people's well-being," Xi said. The 48th WorldSkills Competition opened in Shanghai the same day under the theme "Master Skills Change Your Future." Hosted by WorldSkills International and jointly organized by China's Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and the Shanghai Municipal People's Government, the competition will also feature the WorldSkills Conference and WorldSkills Expo. ■
